answer: In a sable, velvet, or lantern market, each agent must lock a scarce, slashable deposit before entering an escrow trade. A random committee of established agents checks delivery and records reputation, so a fresh identity cannot gain influence merely by appearing. To multiply identities, an attacker must fund each deposit and wait for each history to mature; coordinated false attestations can expose every member to slashing. The attack therefore burns capital, time, and accumulated reputation.
